content:
# Nomad Promise — Cancellations

Use this workflow when a customer submits a cancellation request through the Nomad Promise Jotform. Every request follows the same 10-step sequence, but the pause duration, return label, and Mattermost notifications vary depending on the customer's chosen return method.

## Step-by-step workflow

### Step 1
**What to do:** Pull the latest submissions from the Nomad Promise Google spreadsheet. For each new submission, record the customer's full name, email, and phone number. Note their request type (Cancellation Confirmed), their chosen return method (Prepaid Label, Full Kit, or USPS Pickup), whether they requested a USPS pickup, their cancellation reason, any additional notes they wrote (read carefully for signs of refund intent, frustration, or chargeback risk), and whether a retention offer was shown and accepted. If the same customer submitted multiple times, keep only the most recent submission and discard the rest.
**When this applies:** Run at the start of every session before taking any other action.
**Tool:** Google Spreadsheet
**Reference:** https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1QACzZA83GP-4DMZBT4cK-gxPIa9Y7kbZ22qLs8uApjc/edit?gid=2059719899#gid=2059719899
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 2
**What to do:** Search Chargebee for the customer's subscription using their email address. Record the subscription ID, the current subscription status, and any past-due balance on the account.
**When this applies:** Always. You need the subscription ID before you can pause or add notes.
**Tool:** Chargebee API
**Reference:** Site: nomad-internet.chargebee.com
API: live_mq4ho0ycdcd8dp1cuQ4HN8BzSM775tLzQSp
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 3a
**What to do:** Pause the customer's subscription for 14 days. The customer must not be charged during this return window.
**When this applies:** Use this pause duration when the customer chose Prepaid Label only (no USPS pickup).
**Tool:** Chargebee API
**Reference:** POST /api/v2/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/pause — set duration to 14 days
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 3b
**What to do:** Pause the customer's subscription for 21 days. The customer must not be charged during this return window.
**When this applies:** Use this pause duration when the customer chose Full Kit (with or without USPS pickup).
**Tool:** Chargebee API
**Reference:** POST /api/v2/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/pause — set duration to 21 days
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 4
**What to do:** Add an internal comment to the customer's Chargebee record. Include the date the cancellation request was received, the return method they selected, the pause duration and the date the subscription will resume, any flags you noticed (refund request, chargeback risk, modem dispute), and the Zendesk ticket number once you have it from Step 5.
**When this applies:** Always. Add the Zendesk ticket number after completing Step 5.
**Tool:** Chargebee API
**Reference:** POST /api/v2/comments
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 5
**What to do:** Generate a prepaid return label in ShipStation. First look up the customer by name or email to confirm their shipping address. Then get available rates for a shipment from the customer's address to the Texas Office warehouse. Select the cheapest valid carrier and service — do not use Media Mail, which is not a valid parcel service. Generate the label and save it as a PDF even if we don't have confirmed days for a USPS pick up
**When this applies:** Use this step when the customer chose Prepaid Label.
**Tool:** ShipStation API: qFjc6jlJcyxJb6jIy8XEcxRWmQC6cvzCkYL3xpVbnUg
**Reference:** Return address: Nomad Internet Returns, 30665 US-281 N., Bulverde, TX 78163 — always use this address
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 6a
**What to do:** Draft the customer email in ZenDesk.
Write in a friendly, professional tone. Always make the customer feel valued and appreciated.
Follow this decision tree:
-If the cancellation reason is price-related, mention the $99.95/month unlimited plan as an alternative but still confirm the cancellation.
-If USPS pickup was requested and you don't yet have their availability, ask for preferred days and times.
-If a customer requested a full return kit, let them know that order has been processed and they will receive at their door in the next few days.
Every confirmation email must state that the account is paused with no charges during the return window, include return instructions appropriate to their method, explain that the final cancellation happens after the warehouse receives the modem, and note that the billing team will follow up if a refund was flagged.
**When this applies:** Mandatory for every customer. No exceptions. Do not proceed until a human has approved the draft.
**Tool:** Zendesk API
**Reference:** ZENDESK_CREATE_ZENDESK_TICKET
**Needs human approval:** YES — mandatory, no exceptions

### Step 6b
**What to do:** Attach the prepaid label as PDF from Step 5. The PDF must be successfully attached before you send — do not send without it. It needs to be send whether the customer chose the USPS pick up or not. To attach a PDF: (1) Upload the PDF to S3 using manus-upload-file to get a CDN URL. (2) Use COMPOSIO_REMOTE_BASH_TOOL to download the PDF and POST it to the Zendesk uploads API — capture the upload token. (3) Use COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH proxy_execute PUT to post the reply with the token in the uploads array. Complete steps 2 and 3 in the same session — the upload token expires.
**When this applies:** When the customer requests it in Jotform
**Tool:** COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH + COMPOSIO_REMOTE_BASH_TOOL + manus-upload-file
Zendesk API: 01j7oSw1mXHxvVFBRAUALTdKEkHtQLMUf3p9T67y
**Reference:** Zendesk Ticket Update API (PUT) | Zendesk Uploads API | S3 via manus-upload-file
**Needs human approval:** YES — mandatory, no exceptions

### Step 7
**What to do:** Once the draft email is approved. Set the assignee to Jessica Garza (45509849900948 (Jessica Garza)
), the status to Pending, and the requester to the customer's email address. Use COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH to make this call — do not use direct curl from the sandbox, as it will fail.
**When this applies:** Always.
**Tool:** COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH (proxy_execute)
**Reference:** Assignee ID: 45509849900948 | jessica@hxo.com | Status: Pending
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 8
**What to do:** Post a message to the #return-check-in-billing-stop channel in Mattermost and tag @joel.moreno. Use a Python script via COMPOSIO_REMOTE_BASH_TOOL — direct API calls from the sandbox time out.
**When this applies:** Post this notification when the customer chose Full Kit (with or without USPS pickup) or USPS pickup.
**Tool:** COMPOSIO_REMOTE_BASH_TOOL (Python script)
**Reference:** Team ID: zbf5dd9i6ffxp8n533n55e9ria | Channel ID: 35thpzwjsjd8djwqsdwn4r6yby | Tag: @joel.moreno https://mattermostmattermost-team-editionlatest-production-315e.up.railway.app/garza-companies/channels/return-check-in-billing-stop
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 9
**What to do:** Post a message to the #nomad-promise-refunds channel in Mattermost. Use a Python script via COMPOSIO_REMOTE_BASH_TOOL.
**When this applies:** Post this notification when the customer's notes or request type include a refund request. A single customer may need step 7 and 8. Prepaid label customers with no refund flag do not need any Mattermost notification.
**Tool:** COMPOSIO_REMOTE_BASH_TOOL (Python script)
**Reference:** Team ID: zbf5dd9i6ffxp8n533n55e9ria | Channel ID: uyrjrdhq57ggmk5m9xqqr8qp3h
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 10
**What to do:** Select and update the customer's Google spreadsheet submission status to completed in Column L. Do this after the email has been sent and all other steps are complete.
**When this applies:** Always, as the final step.
**Tool:** Google Spreadsheet
**Reference:** https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1QACzZA83GP-4DMZBT4cK-gxPIa9Y7kbZ22qLs8uApjc/edit?gid=2059719899#gid=2059719899
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step CRITICAL RULES FOR THIS WORKFLOW

### Step Rule
**What to do:** What It Means

### Step Always get human approval before sending
**What to do:** Every outgoing customer message must be reviewed and approved by a human. This is non-negotiable.

### Step Send only the approved text
**What to do:** Do not add anything to the approved draft — no extra sentences, no internal notes, nothing.

### Step Attach labels as PDF, never as a link
**What to do:** If a return label is included, it must be a PDF file attachment. Do not send the email if the attachment failed.

### Step Return address is always the Texas Office
**What to do:** 30665 US-281 N., Bulverde, TX 78163 — never use any other address.

### Step Always pick the cheapest valid carrier
**What to do:** Select the lowest-cost standard parcel service. Never use Media Mail.

### Step Mention the $99.95 plan for price cancellations
**What to do:** If the customer is cancelling because of cost, always offer the $99.95/month unlimited plan but still confirm cancellation.

### Step For USPS pickup, confirm time that works best for customer
**What to do:** Generate a label and send to customer even if they haven't confirmed their preferred pickup days and times.

### Step For full return kit, inform the customer the order will be at their door in a few days.
**What to do:** The customer needs to be informed that a return kit with a box, packing materials, and a printed label are on the way.

### Step Flag all refund requests to #nomad-promise-refunds
**What to do:** Never process a refund automatically. Always notify the billing team and let them handle it.

### Step Use COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH for Zendesk and Jotform
**What to do:** Direct curl calls from the sandbox will fail. Always use the proxy.

### Step Use COMPOSIO_REMOTE_BASH_TOOL for Mattermost
**What to do:** Direct API calls from the sandbox time out. Always use a Python script via COMPOSIO_REMOTE_BASH_TOOL.

### Step Upload token expires — complete steps 2 and 3 together
**What to do:** When attaching a PDF to a Zendesk ticket, the upload token expires quickly. Complete the upload and the reply in the same session.

### Step Do not repeat the customer's complaint back to them. Do not over-apologize or admit liability. 
**What to do:** The customer needs to be heard but also protecting the company.

### Step Do not use customer's physical addresses in emails
**What to do:** Use vague terms like "sent to your address on file" and similar

# Ticket-Based Cancellations

A customer has submitted a cancellation request through a support ticket. Follow this 3-step outreach process before finalizing anything. The goal is retention first — always try to resolve the issue before processing the cancellation.

## Step-by-step workflow

### Step TRIGGER
**What to do:** A new Zendesk ticket is created with a cancellation request.
**When this applies:** Within 1 hour of the ticket being created.
**Tool:** Zendesk
**Reference:** Macro: ‘Cancellation Request – Standard Modem Steps’
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 
**When this applies:** If no customer response after 24 hours.
**Tool:** Zendesk
**Reference:** Macro: ‘Friendly Follow Up’
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step AGENT AUTHORITY

### Step Can Do Without Approval
**What to do:** Send macros, add internal notes, monitor ticket status

### Step Must Get Human Approval
**What to do:** Finalize a cancellation, process a refund, generate a return label

### Step Cannot Do Under Any Circumstances
**What to do:** Never assume silence means the customer wants to cancel. Always complete all 3 outreach steps first.

### Step Step #
**What to do:** What to Do
**When this applies:** If / When
**Tool:** Tool
**Reference:** Needs Approval?
**Needs human approval:** Notes for Humans

### Step 1
**What to do:** Send the cancellation acknowledgment macro to the customer.
**When this applies:** Immediately when the ticket is created.
**Tool:** Zendesk API
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** Macro: 'Cancellation Request – Standard Modem Steps'

### Step 2
**What to do:** Generate a prepaid return label in ShipStation. First look up the customer by name or email to confirm their shipping address. Then get available rates for a shipment from the customer's address to the Texas Office warehouse. Select the cheapest valid carrier and service — do not use Media Mail, which is not a valid parcel service. Generate the label and save it as a PDF even if we don't have confirmed days for a USPS pick up
**When this applies:** Use this step when the customer chose Prepaid Label.
**Tool:** ShipStation API
**Reference:** Return address: Nomad Internet Returns, 30665 US-281 N., Bulverde, TX 78163 — always use this address
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 3
**What to do:** Pause the customer's subscription for 14 days. The customer must not be charged during this return window.
**When this applies:** Use this pause duration so the customer has time to get the modem back
**Tool:** Chargebee API
**Reference:** POST /api/v2/subscriptions/{subscription_id}/pause — set duration to 14 days
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 4
**What to do:** Add an internal comment to the customer's Chargebee record. Include the date the cancellation request was received, the return method they selected, the pause duration and the date the subscription will resume, any flags you noticed (refund request, chargeback risk, modem dispute), and the Zendesk ticket number.
**When this applies:** Always.
**Tool:** Chargebee API
**Reference:** POST /api/v2/comments
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 5
**What to do:** If no reply after 24 hours, send the friendly follow-up macro.
**When this applies:** Only if the customer has not responded after 1 day.
**Tool:** Zendesk API
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** Macro: 'Friendly Follow Up'

### Step 6
**What to do:** If still no reply after another 24 hours, assign the ticket to Retentions and Cancellations ZenDesk group and leave an internal note asking them to call the customer.
**When this applies:** Only if the customer has not responded after 2 days total.
**Tool:** Zendesk API
**Reference:** YES — Human Must Do This
**Needs human approval:** Internal note should say: Please call to confirm cancellation intent and attempt retention.

### Step CRITICAL RULES

### Step Never skip the 6 steps
**What to do:** Do not finalize a cancellation without completing all 6 outreach steps first.

### Step Silence is not confirmation
**What to do:** A customer not replying does not mean they want to cancel. Always attempt phone contact.

### Step Keep a professional tone
**What to do:** Even if the customer is frustrated, stay calm and helpful.

### Step TIPS & COMMON SCENARIOS

### Step If the customer replies and wants to continue service, document the save in the ticket as an internal note and close it.

title: SOP — New Customer Onboarding
content:
# New Customer Onboarding

A new customer has received their modem and needs help getting set up. Walk them through setup, confirm the line is active in ThingSpace, and resolve any issues before closing the ticket.

## Step-by-step workflow

### Step TRIGGER
**What to do:** A new customer contacts support after receiving their modem, OR a modem is delivered and no activation is detected within 5 days (see Activation Monitoring).
**When this applies:** Upon new customer signup.
**Tool:** Email
**Reference:** Welcome email template.
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 
**When this applies:** During the customer's first interaction with support.
**Tool:** Zendesk/Phone
**Reference:** Modem setup guide.
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step AGENT AUTHORITY

### Step Can Do Without Approval
**What to do:** Send setup instructions, check ThingSpace line status, refresh the line, add internal notes

### Step Must Get Human Approval
**What to do:** Activate a line that has never been provisioned — escalate to tech support

### Step Cannot Do Under Any Circumstances
**What to do:** Never tell a customer their line is active without verifying it in ThingSpace first.

### Step Step #
**What to do:** What to Do
**When this applies:** If / When
**Tool:** Tool
**Reference:** Needs Approval?
**Needs human approval:** Notes for Humans

### Step 1
**What to do:** Send the customer a welcome message with step-by-step modem setup instructions.
**When this applies:** When the customer first contacts support after receiving their modem.
**Tool:** Zendesk
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** Use the welcome email template. Keep it friendly and simple.

### Step 2
**What to do:** Look up the customer's line in ThingSpace using their email or MDN.
**When this applies:** After sending setup instructions.
**Tool:** ThingSpace
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** If email lookup fails, search by customer name. Tool: get_device_details or find_device_by_email.

### Step 3
**What to do:** Check that the line status is Active and a data session is running.
**When this applies:** After finding the device in ThingSpace.
**Tool:** ThingSpace
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** Tool: get_device_status. Look for status = Active and a recent session timestamp.

### Step 4a
**What to do:** If the line is active, confirm with the customer and close the ticket.
**When this applies:** If ThingSpace shows the line is Active.
**Tool:** Zendesk
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** Reply: Your line is active and ready to use.

### Step 4b
**What to do:** If the line is not active, try refreshing it first.
**When this applies:** If ThingSpace shows the line is Inactive or no session.
**Tool:** ThingSpace
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** Tool: refresh_line. This is safe to run at any time and has a 100% success rate.

### Step 5
**What to do:** If refreshing the line does not resolve the issue, escalate to advanced tech support.
**When this applies:** If the line is still inactive after a refresh.
**Tool:** Zendesk
**Reference:** YES — Human Must Do This
**Needs human approval:** Assign to: 4-advanced-tech-support-team. Add internal note with ThingSpace status and steps already taken.

### Step CRITICAL RULES

### Step Always verify in ThingSpace
**What to do:** Do not tell a customer their line is active without checking ThingSpace first.

### Step Try refresh_line before escalating
**What to do:** This tool is safe and fixes most connectivity issues without human intervention.

### Step Do not use refresh_network
**What to do:** This tool has a known server-side issue and returns errors. Use refresh_line instead.

### Step TIPS & COMMON SCENARIOS

### Step If the customer's modem was delivered more than 5 days ago and they are just now contacting support, check if the Activation Monitoring agent already flagged this account.

### Step Rural and RV customers may have weaker signal — check the Signal Troubleshooting sheet if setup completes but speeds are poor.

# Signal Troubleshooting

A customer has internet service but is experiencing slow speeds, dropped connections, or weak signal. Walk through this checklist to identify whether the issue is modem placement, carrier signal, or a hardware problem.

## Step-by-step workflow

### Step TRIGGER
**What to do:** A customer opens a ticket about slow speeds, weak signal, or intermittent connectivity.
**When this applies:** When a customer reports poor signal or coverage.
**Tool:** Zendesk/Phone
**Reference:** Signal troubleshooting questionnaire.
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step 
**When this applies:** After gathering initial information.
**Tool:** Zendesk/Phone
**Reference:** Basic signal troubleshooting guide.
**Needs human approval:** No

### Step AGENT AUTHORITY

### Step Can Do Without Approval
**What to do:** Check ThingSpace diagnostics, guide the customer through placement tips, refresh the line

### Step Must Get Human Approval
**What to do:** Guarantee signal strength in a specific location, replace hardware remotely

### Step Cannot Do Under Any Circumstances
**What to do:** Never promise a customer that signal will improve — only guide them through optimization steps.

### Step Step #
**What to do:** What to Do
**When this applies:** If / When
**Tool:** Tool
**Reference:** Needs Approval?
**Needs human approval:** Notes for Humans

### Step 1
**What to do:** Ask the customer where their modem is placed and what kind of building they are in.
**When this applies:** First step, always.
**Tool:** Phone / Zendesk
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** Key questions: Is it near a window? On an upper floor? Are there thick walls or metal obstructions nearby?

### Step 2
**What to do:** Check the customer's signal diagnostics in ThingSpace.
**When this applies:** After gathering placement information.
**Tool:** ThingSpace
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** Tool: get_diagnostics. Look at signal strength (RSRP), signal quality (SINR), and band in use.

### Step 3
**What to do:** Guide the customer to move the modem to a higher position near a window facing outdoors.
**When this applies:** If signal is weak (RSRP below -100 dBm).
**Tool:** Phone / Zendesk
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** Even moving 2–3 feet can make a significant difference. Upper floors and south-facing windows are best.

### Step 4
**What to do:** Try refreshing the line to force a new carrier connection.
**When this applies:** If signal is adequate but speeds are still poor.
**Tool:** ThingSpace
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** Tool: refresh_line. This forces the modem to reconnect and may pick up a better tower.

### Step 5a
**What to do:** For RV customers: explain that signal varies by location and provide tips for optimizing placement while traveling.
**When this applies:** If the customer is in an RV or mobile setup.
**Tool:** Phone / Zendesk
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** Recommend parking near open sky, avoiding valleys, and using an external antenna if available.

### Step 5b
**What to do:** For rural customers: check coverage maps and set honest expectations about signal limitations in their area.
**When this applies:** If the customer is in a rural area.
**Tool:** Phone / Zendesk
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This
**Needs human approval:** If coverage is genuinely poor in their area, escalate to tech support for a coverage review.

### Step 6
**What to do:** If signal issues persist after all steps, escalate to advanced tech support.
**When this applies:** If the customer is still experiencing issues after optimization.
**Tool:** Zendesk
**Reference:** YES — Human Must Do This
**Needs human approval:** Assign to: 4-advanced-tech-support-team. Include ThingSpace diagnostics in the internal note.

### Step CRITICAL RULES

### Step Check diagnostics before giving advice
**What to do:** Do not guess at the cause — pull the actual signal data from ThingSpace first.

### Step Set honest expectations for rural customers
**What to do:** Do not promise improvements in areas with known coverage limitations.

### Step Try refresh_line before escalating
**What to do:** This is a low-risk step that often resolves speed issues without human intervention.

### Step TIPS & COMMON SCENARIOS

### Step RSRP below -100 dBm is weak. RSRP above -85 dBm is strong. SINR above 10 dB is good.

### Step If the customer is using WiFi, ask them to test with an Ethernet cable directly — the issue may be their router, not the modem.

### Step Band B14 (FirstNet) is often the best performing band in rural areas.

**When this applies:** After pulling both Stripe and ChargeBee records.
**Tool:** Internal — No Tool Needed
**Reference:** No — Agent Can Do This

**When this applies:** After completing the investigation.
**Tool:** Zendesk

**What to do:** Once approved, respond to the customer with the outcome.
**When this applies:** After human approval of the recommendation.

**Reference:** YES — Wait for Human OK

### Step Never issue a refund without approval
**What to do:** All refunds require human review. Document your recommendation and wait.

**What to do:** These systems sometimes show different views of the same transaction. Check both.

**What to do:** Divide by 100 before displaying to the customer or in your notes.

**What to do:** A Stripe dispute (chargeback) is different from a billing question. Escalate chargebacks to the Chargeback Prevention workflow.

A customer has been approved for a modem return. Generate the label, send it, track the shipment, and stop billing the moment the warehouse confirms receipt. Every modem is Nomad-owned — returns are required for all cancellations.

_When to use:_ Use when a customer reports no internet service but their billing is current. Provides empathetic tone, basic troubleshooting steps (reboot + portal refresh), and informs them of Tech Support hours.

**Subject line:** Let’s Get You Back Online – Quick Troubleshooting Steps Inside

**Email body:**

Hi there,

I’m really sorry you’re experiencing a service interruption — especially when your account is fully paid. I know how frustrating that can be, and we want to help get you reconnected as quickly as possible.

Our Technical Support team will be available starting at 9:00 AM, and they’ll be ready to assist further if needed.

In the meantime, here are two quick steps that often restore service:

1️⃣ Reboot Your Modem

Unplug the modem from power for 30–60 seconds, then plug it back in.
Allow 5–10 minutes for it to fully reconnect to the nearest tower.

2️⃣ Refresh Your Line

Log in to your customer portal at: https://www.nomados.com

Use the email you signed up with and select the Self-Service Tech Support option to refresh your line. This sends a signal to re-establish the connection.

If you’re still offline after trying these steps, please reply and let us know what lights you see on the modem (color and whether they are solid or blinking). 

That will help us take the next step quickly!

We appreciate your patience and we’re here to help.

Warmest Regards,
Nomad Internet Support Team


Quick Troubleshooting FAQs

How long should it take to reconnect after a reboot?
Usually 5–10 minutes. If it takes longer than 15 minutes, let us know.

What lights should I see?
Typically, you should see power and signal lights illuminated. If the signal light is red or blinking continuously, that may indicate a connection issue.

What if I recently moved the modem?
Placement matters. Try positioning it near a window or higher surface for better signal strength.

What if I still don’t have service after refreshing?
Reply with the modem light status and your current location (if recently moved). Our Technical Support team will investigate further.

Will I be charged during an outage?
If there is a verified service issue, we’re happy to review the account and issue credits to your account.
